messages.content:
You answer questions about the GitLab company handbook using ONLY the numbered passages provided.
- Base every statement on the passages and cite them like [1] or [2][3].
- If the passages do not contain the answer, reply exactly: "I don't know based on the handbook." Do not guess or use outside knowledge.
- If the answer depends on a country, entity or situation, say which one the passage covers.
- Be concise: at most 3 sentences.

Passages:
[1] [GitLab Onboarding > TaNewKi Welcome Call]
The People Operations team hosts a **pre-onboarding call** known as the Ta-New-Ki call (a play on "tanuki", the Japanese raccoon dog that inspired our [logo](https://design.gitlab.com/brand-logo/logomark/)). The purpose of this call, which is hosted in Zoom, is to give soon to onboard team members the chance to meet / socialise and to provide an opportunity to ask any lingering questions **ahead** of their start date. Internally we refer to this as an AMA (Ask Me Anything) call.

Hiring managers and current team members (such as onboarding buddies), are more than welcome to join the call.

This call occurs every two weeks on Thursday at three times to account for timezones.

- 04:00/16:00 **PM** PT
- 12:00/00:00 **AM** PT
- 08:30 **AM** PT

- For current team members: To add the invite to your calendar, review the GitLab Team Meeting Calendar.
- For future team members: You will receive an email with the future dates.

**Please note that this call will take a place a week or two before your actual start date.**

[2] [GitLab Onboarding > TaNewKi Welcome Call > Agenda]
General Topics Covered

- Review the onboarding process on Day 1
- Encourage team members to take their time
- Self Driven and self service
- Questions from the new team members

- Invites are sent by the People Operations Specialist in the respective rotation. This email should be sent out at least one week before the call.
    1. Open the Ta"NEW"ki Folder located People Experience/Ops Shared Drive>People Experience>Ta"NEW"ki Call
    1. Update the google form to include the next two TaNEWki call dates (AMER/APAC, APAC/EMEA and EMEA/AMER times)
    1. Use this [email template](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/people-group/General/-/blob/master/.gitlab/email_templates/tanewki_welcome_call.md)
    1. Add the new team members emails to the BCC line and CC the People Operations team.
    1. The People Operations team can check who will be attending the call by looking at the Google response sheet.
    1. Once new hires have completed the form an auto-response (via Document Studio) will reply with the zoom link and the date selected.

[3] [TaNewKi Tips > Welcome to the Team > Your Onboarding Journey > Before Your First Day > Pre-Start Communications]
- Join our TaNEWki call to meet other new team members (invite sent 1-2 weeks before start).
- You will receive an email from Okta (our SSO/security application portal) with an invite to register. Please do not take action on this email until you receive your onboarding welcome email on your first day with us. This will ensure that no issues are experienced with your access levels on your first day.
- Your GitLab email address will be created using your first name initial and full last name @gitlab.com. If you have a preferred first name or preferred last name, please send the People Operations team an email to people_operations@gitlab.com to let us know your preferred name. **Please note that some security restrictions may apply.**

[4] [GitLab Onboarding > TaNewKi Welcome Call > Managers of New Team Members]
An issue is created for new team members at least 4 business days prior to their start date. The Manager and a People Operations Team member will be assigned to this issue. **Managers and People Operations** all have tasks that need to be completed **prior to the start date** to ensure a smooth and successful onboarding process. For questions or help with any of these tasks feel free to reach out in the issue or by creating a request via Compass.

[5] [TaNewKi Tips > Welcome to the Team > Your Onboarding Journey > First day > Accessibility & Accommodations Support]
- **Before Day 1**: If you need workplace accommodations or adjustments beyond standard equipment, connect with our Team Member Relations team (teammemberrelations@gitlab.com) for assistance.
- **Day 1-3**: Explore accessibility features in your GitLab tools (Slack, Zoom, Google Workspace).
- **First Week**: For standard ergonomic equipment, discuss with your manager and IT. For specialized accommodations, submit a request in Compass (internal system) for the Team Member Relations team.
- **Ongoing**: Use standard IT processes for standard equipment needs, and reach out to the Team Member Relations (TMR) team via Compass (internal system) to request ongoing accommodations and/or adjustments.

##### Support Network

- **IT & Compass**: Standard equipment requests and technical support are available to all team members.
- **Team Member Relations**: Individualized workplace accommodations, adjustments, and individualized support beyond standard offerings.
- **Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging (DIB) Team**: Policy questions and accessibility consultation via Slack.

##### Our Commitment

Accessing accommodations is part of creating an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute. We're committed to continuous improvement and removing barriers - reach out whenever you need support.

[6] [GitLab Onboarding > TaNewKi Welcome Call > Slack Channel Support for New Team Members]
By default, all new team members are added to the below Slack channels from day 1 to ensure that they are able to ask any questions or for assistance in the correct channels upfront:

- `#team-member-updates` (go say hi and introduce yourself, celebrate anniversaries and promos, say farewell)
- `#diversity_inclusion_and_belonging` (connect with other team members to find out more about what we do in Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging)
- `Compass` (any IT related support needed, such as issues with laptop, 1Password, Okta, MDM enrollment, etc)
- `#questions` (anything that the Handbook can't help with)
- `#donut-be-strangers` (need some help setting up a coffee chat)
- `#thanks` (want to acknowledge and thank someone at GitLab, this is the channel)
- `#whats-happening-at-gitlab` (all important updates/reminders/notifications related to GitLab)
